newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SIAULIU BANK Q1 97 NET PROFIT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SIAULIU BANK Q1 97 NET PROFIT DOWN.

text.p: Lithuania's Siauliu Bank said on Thursday its net profit dipped to 360,000 litas in the first quarter of 1997 versus 1.57 million litas in Q1 1996.
Donatas Savickas, deputy chairman of Siauliu Bank, told Reuters that the assets of the bank rose to 77.6 million litas in the first quarter from 71.8 million at the end of 1996.
The loan porfolio went up to 50.8 million in the first quarter of 1997 versus 42.2 million at the end of last year, Savickas said.
He added that deposits at the end of the first three months were 47.6 million litas versus 42.3 million at end 1996.
The bank earlier reported a 3.99 million litas audited net profit for 1996.
The shareholders' meeting last month said it aimed for a net profit of around eight million litas in 1997.

"Although our first quarter results are below target we expect the new 14 million litas share issue which is to be registered with the securities commission in the near future will help improve our activity," Savickas said.
Siauliu's share capital is currently 20 million litas.

Present shareholders will have priority subscription rights for the news shares and the rest will be sold to the Lithuanian Development Bank, Baltic Fund or Majid Al Ibrahim, the representative of the Saudi Arabian Royal family, Savickas said.
Present shareholders, Hermis Bank among them, have no more than a 10 percent stake in the bank, Savickas added.
"Hopes for sucessful operations at the bank are linked with the Siauliai free economic zone which is supposed to be registered this year," Savickas said.
